verdict.rationale: Mem0's docs show that the product itself extracts individual facts from raw conversation turns sent to `add`, and it automatically organizes memories into a graph without a user-defined schema. Community users corroborate that it stores facts drawn from conversations. However, nothing documents background consolidation, such as merging, deduplicating or updating existing memories asynchronously, or how it judges what is salient versus discarded. missing for 10: documented background/asynchronous consolidation or deduplication of memories, explicit description of salience filtering (what is kept vs dropped), hands-on corroboration of extraction quality.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the memory layer decides for itself what is worth remembering — extracting salient facts from raw conversation and consolidating them in the background

citations.quote: Mem0 pulls the individual facts out of the conversation and stores each one separately
You send conversation turns to `add`, then call `search` before the next model request to fetch relevant context.
Mem0 Platform automatically organizes your memories into a graph... without you defining any schema.
storing facts from conversations — 'user prefers Python,' 'user is vegetarian.'
